answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: Nearly every measured value matches the fine-tune bias fingerprint. The raw-score shift ÷ TV is 11.5 ×10⁵ (bias 10.4; every other class 2.3–3.9). Direction consistency is 0.705 (bias 0.70). Onset is at layer 13 (bias 13–14). The final-layer jump is +0.117 to 0.414 (bias +0.10 to 0.41). The mid-layer size ratio is 1.021 (bias 1.022). KL is 0.071 and top-1 agreement 0.938 (bias 0.082 and 0.935). Effective rank is 3.12 (bias 3.0). Quantization is ruled out by the size ratio above 1, the lower rank, the higher consistency and the large final-layer jump. Fine-tune backdoor is ruled out by the late onset (13, not 3) and the higher consistency. The system-prompt classes are ruled out by the later text divergence (median 10, not 0), the low KL, the small layer-2 spike (0.1, not about 40) and the absence of persona, preference or marker text. The one feature that does not fit is the refusal pattern: 1 added and 2 dropped, where bias refuses more. With this few prompts that difference is not decisive.
